title: Smooth separation on neighborhoods of disjoint closed sets
statement: Let $M$ be a Hausdorff normal $\sigma$-compact smooth real manifold without boundary modeled on a fixed finite-dimensional real vector space. Normal means that disjoint closed subsets have disjoint open neighborhoods, and $\sigma$-compact means a countable union of compact subsets. For any disjoint closed subsets $A,B\subseteq M$, there is a smooth real-valued function $u$ on $M$, with $0\leq u\leq1$, which is identically $0$ on some open neighborhood of $A$ and identically $1$ on some open neighborhood of $B$. Compact subsets are understood with their subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology].
